component: Incumbent inventory for /correct (repeated-mistake-class sweep and structural-fix ladder) on the global dotfiles harness
purpose: Map each /correct mechanism to what this harness already has, with control surface and file:line, or NONE. Also say where operator corrections of agent behaviour are captured today and what consumes them.
mechanism:
Per-mechanism map. A covering mechanism is cited only where I read the line. Everything else is NONE.

1. MINE HISTORY FOR REPEATED MISTAKE CLASSES: NONE for operator corrections of behaviour.
 - Nearest: papercut counts repeats by distinct sessions (bin/papercut.py:15-21, "rollup counts signatures over a window, ranks by how many DISTINCT sessions hit them"). Control surface: `papercut list --days N`, `papercut rollup`, `papercut triage` (skills-local/papercut/SKILL.md:104-112, 142).
 - It covers a different input. Hard tool failures come from the PostToolUseFailure hook. Voluntary friction comes from `papercut add`. SKILL.md:16-24 limits the voluntary class to friction with "no error signature": wrong docs, silent-wrong output, stale caches, hostile tools. A correction such as "don't do X" is not tool friction and has no failure signature, so nothing feeds it.
 - papercut mining of "the current session" runs only when asked (SKILL.md:378-384), only for tool friction, and is not git-history mining.
 - HARNESS.md:236 denial-mine.py mines `toolDenialKind` records. It assigns a "behavioral" bucket (denial-mine.py:59, 132, "guards coach ... config cannot fix intent"). That is permission/guard denials, not operator corrections, and the weekly toast deliberately excludes the bucket (HARNESS.md:236).
 - I found no git-history, revert or commit-message miner. My grep of the harness for correction handling in memory-mine files returned nothing, and memory-mine.py is not at bin/memory-mine.py. The memory-mine path is unverified.

2. FOUR-LEVEL FIX LADDER (architecture > lint/test > skill/rule > human review): PARTIAL, one rung-subset, pointed at the wrong object.
 - rent-check RUBRIC.md:185-191 (E2) routes invariants to the "cheapest deterministic layer that fully covers them: linter/CI for code shape, PreToolUse-style hooks for tool use, permission config for access". Control surface: user-invoked `/rent-check [path]` (SKILL.md:10-11 has disable-model-invocation).
 - E2 and E1 (RUBRIC.md:179-184) classify RULES IN CONTEXT FILES. SKILL.md:21-29 scopes it to "always-loaded" context files and their surrounding surface. They do not take a repeated mistake as input.
 - E2 has no "eliminate by architecture / unrepresentable state" rung. Its first rung is linter/CI.
 - papercut dossier field `## Cheapest remedy` (papercut.py:366, template line 854-855, DOSSIER_JUDGMENT_FIELDS at 360-372) is an operator-filled prose slot. It enforces non-emptiness only (SKILL.md:157-158, adopt exits 2). It has no ladder and no ordering of remedy strength. Its input is a tool-friction family.
 - CLAUDE.md "Diagnose root causes, not symptoms. No band-aid patches..." is prose with no enforcer (digest line 18; not re-read by me). The chokepoint doc (docs/solutions/best-practices/instrument-at-the-chokepoint-that-already-sees-the-cause.md:43-49) is a placement doctrine for instrumentation, not a fix ladder, and has no control surface.

3. PROVE EACH NEW CHECK FAILS ON A REAL PAST MISTAKE: PARTIAL, as separate pieces and never as one step.
 - papercut dossier `## Planted negative` and `## Acceptance Criteria` (papercut.py:367, 369). Fields are required non-empty only. adopt exit 2 names missing fields (SKILL.md:157-158, 225-228). Nothing runs the planted negative.
 - papercut work-spec gate: WORK_SPEC_SECTIONS = Acceptance Criteria, Planted negative, No-Claim Boundary (papercut.py:86). Consumer is `work-spec-check.sh`, which gates adopt (SKILL.md:373-374).
 - rent-check SKILL.md:108-112: the engine ships `bin/rent-check.test.py`, "asserting it fires on known-bad input as well as passing on known-good". That tests rent-check's own checks, not a check built for a user's mistake.
 - HARNESS.md:49: before adding or widening a git-guard rule, "replay it against 60 days of real Bash-tool commands ... old guard vs new on a scratch feature-branch repo ... report every decision transition". This is the nearest real instance of the mechanism, but it is a doctrine sentence for git-guard rules only.
 - HARNESS.md:227: `dcg-contract` (56 cases) proves guard logic against the live binary.
 - No generic "re-plant a past mistake, show the new check fails" step exists for repository code.

4. RULE-TO-ENFORCER TABLE: PARTIAL, computed per audit and not persisted.
 - rent-check E1 classifies each always/never/must rule as redundant, advisory-only or backing-without-mention (RUBRIC.md:179-184). The engine is `bin/rent-check.py inventory <root> --json` (SKILL.md:100). The output is a per-run report and a ledger, with receipts in the newest run directory (SKILL.md:81-87).
 - HARNESS.md:46 is a prose-to-enforcer map for ONE section only. It explicitly refuses to transcribe entries: "Do not transcribe entries into prose", with live jq counts instead.
 - harness-doctor check 11 (HARNESS.md:46) detects drift of settings and hooks. It does not map rules to enforcers.
 - Open defect: rent-check writes to the target repo (#1244, from the digest, not re-verified).

5. EXCEPTIONS WITH REASON / EXPIRY / APPROVER: NONE as a generic mechanism.
 - papercut `family dispose --verdict intended-policy|insufficient-evidence|upstream-reported` (SKILL.md:232-240) records a reasoned disposition, and `family reopen` reverses it. It covers a friction family, has no expiry and no named approver, and is not an exception to a check.
 - git-guard escape hatches such as `ALLOW_AI_TRAILER=1` (HARNESS.md:49) are per-rule env escapes. They are not a registry and have no expiry.
 - HARNESS.md:69 records an operator ruling with a date. That is a log convention and not an exception register.

6. DROP RULES ONCE ENFORCEMENT MAKES THEM IMPOSSIBLE: PARTIAL.
 - rent-check E1 "redundant: ... prune the prose, keep a one-line pointer" and the verdicts CUT/DEMOTE (RUBRIC.md:179-184; SKILL.md:6-9). Control surface: `/rent-check`, which proposes diffs and never auto-applies. The trigger is a periodic audit, not a new enforcer.
 - HARNESS.md:56-59 shows it done by hand: "Demoted from CLAUDE.md (2026-09-21, dotfiles#1286)".
 - papercut `family dispose` / `close-observed` closes the loop on friction families, and the `verified` stage needs "no recurrence while capture was alive" (SKILL.md:309-342).
 - Prior art on the failure mode: rent-check E4 paper-tiger gates (RUBRIC.md:198-202).

7. TRIGGER ON EVERY OPERATOR CORRECTION: NONE.
 - No hook in the digest's settings.json hook inventory (digest line 5: UserPromptSubmit 1, Stop 2, no SessionEnd) was shown to detect a correction. I did not read the UserPromptSubmit hook, so its content is unverified.
 - papercut SKILL.md:378-384 says to mine a session "only when asked ... not something to run on your own initiative at the end of a session".
 - The memory doctrine (given fact) has the model write `feedback` notes. That is model-initiated and relies on judgment, with no deterministic trigger.

SEPARATE QUESTION: where are operator corrections of agent BEHAVIOUR captured today, and what consumes them?
 - Capture: the memory `feedback` type is the only designed home (given fact: "guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why"). Files are memory/<project>/ (digest line 15: 1,095 fleet-wide, 144 for dotfiles). Capture is by the model's own judgment, or by `/memory-mine` (bounded capture). I could not open memory-mine's source (path not at bin/memory-mine.py), so how it detects corrections is unverified.
 - Duplicate doctrine (given fact): "check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate". The effect is to fold a repeated correction into one note and not to escalate it. There is no repeat counter and no promotion trigger. papercut.py:18-21 states the opposite design on purpose: "Duplicates are kept and counted — the inverse of memory-mine.py, which discards a note that overlaps an existing index line".
 - Second route: ce-compound writes docs/solutions learnings (ce-compound SKILL.md:25-29). It is invoked "after work" for a "solved problem" (SKILL.md:3, 31-43), one learning per run. It is a documentation level, not an enforcement level, and its input is a solved problem, not a correction.
 - Consumers: (a) memory loading at session start and recall, which is advisory prose; (b) memory-audit.py triage, weekly `flagged:N`, and the memory-dream consolidation plugin (HARNESS.md:237). These score rot and consolidate, are operator-gated, and are proposal-only. HARNESS.md:237 describes them as consolidation, not as promotion of a note to a hook or lint. I read no consumer that turns a repeated feedback note into an enforcer. rent-check only audits context files (SKILL.md:21-29). Whether it reads memory feedback notes was not verified. Its P3 memory ceilings section (RUBRIC.md:233) concerns size limits.
 - Nothing counts how often the same correction recurs across feedback notes. papercut's cross-session counting is the only such mechanism, and it does not ingest corrections.
 - Net: raw material exists (144 dotfiles feedback notes), but the loop from correction to enforcer is open at the "detect repeat" and "pick strongest level" steps.
fit_and_overlap:
Per /correct mechanism, covering incumbent on this harness and its control surface, or none.
1. Mine history for repeated mistake classes: NONE for behaviour corrections. Nearest is papercut distinct-session ranking, steered by `papercut list/rollup/triage`, but its inputs are tool failures and voluntary friction only (papercut.py:15-21; SKILL.md:16-24).
2. Four-level fix ladder: PARTIAL. rent-check E2 ladder, steered by `/rent-check [path]` (RUBRIC.md:185-191), applies to context-file rules and has no architecture rung. The papercut `## Cheapest remedy` field (papercut.py:366) is unordered free prose.
3. Prove each check fails on a real past mistake: PARTIAL. papercut `## Planted negative` is required non-empty only (papercut.py:369), checked by work-spec-check.sh (SKILL.md:373-374). The HARNESS.md:49 git-guard replay doctrine is the real precedent, for git-guard rules only. Nothing executes a planted negative for repo code.
4. Rule-to-enforcer table: PARTIAL. rent-check E1 run per audit (RUBRIC.md:179-184), not persisted; HARNESS.md:46 covers one section by design.
5. Exceptions with reason / expiry / approver: NONE. papercut `family dispose` (SKILL.md:232-240) has a verdict and reversal but no expiry or approver and applies to friction families. Env escape hatches (HARNESS.md:49) are not a registry.
6. Drop rules once impossible: PARTIAL. rent-check E1 "redundant: prune the prose" and CUT/DEMOTE verdicts, proposal-only, periodic (SKILL.md:6-9; RUBRIC.md:179-184).
7. Trigger on every operator correction: NONE. papercut session mining is "only when asked" (SKILL.md:378-384). Memory capture relies on model judgment.

Overall, no skill performs the sweep: the digest says so (line 31) and my reading found no counter-example. Several pieces are adjacent, and none takes a repeated operator correction as input. Placement implication: the closest home for a new capability is a user-invoked skill (as rent-check is, disable-model-invocation). Extending the papercut dossier is possible but it would change papercut's scope from tool friction to agent behaviour, which SKILL.md:16-24 and :72-81 explicitly draw. The memory doctrine's "update, not escalate" (given fact) points the opposite way from a repeat-driven ladder, so any port would add an escalation step the memory system lacks. This is not a SKIP-as-covered case under the standing rule: no equivalent capability is demonstrably available for this task.
